q: Is steel furniture, such as almirahs, racks and office chairs, covered by CBAM?
title: Is steel furniture covered by CBAM?
short: Not today. Furniture under chapter 94 of the Combined Nomenclature, including metal furniture under 9403 and seats under 9401, is not in Annex I of the EU CBAM Regulation. The steel sheet and tubes you buy are covered when imported into the EU, and a December 2025 proposal may extend CBAM to downstream goods.
audience: Steel furniture, storage and racking exporters

ul: 9401: seats, including office chairs with steel frames: not in Annex I.
9403: other furniture, including metal cupboards, filing cabinets and beds: not in Annex I.
7308: structures and parts of structures of iron or steel: covered. Industrial racking can be classified here; check with the importer.

sections.h: Where you may be pulled in
ul: Warehouse and pallet racking declared as a steel structure under 7308 is covered.
Loose steel parts shipped for assembly in the EU may fall under chapter 73 headings in Annex I.

p: The EU importer declares the 8 digit CN code and customs can reclassify it. Agree the code with your buyer before shipment and keep it on the invoice.
